title: an unsatisfied note is published and writable only by migration -- no verb can author or edit one
body:
An unsatisfied criterion's `note` is published on both faces, writable only by migration, and authorable or editable by NO verb.

## Measured

Every construction of `AcState::Unsatisfied` in `src` (tests excluded):

| site                | value written        |
| ------------------- | -------------------- |
| `legacy.rs:1726`    | `note` (the v2 text) |
| `legacy.rs:1732`    | `note: None`         |
| `legacy.rs:1734`    | `note: None`         |
| `facade.rs:4585`    | `note: None`         |
| `facade.rs:4993`    | `note: None`         |

`grep "note: Some"` across `src` outside `legacy.rs`: **zero**.

`facade.rs:4585` is `AcState::entry`, reached by `ac new` / `ac rescope` / `ac reinstate`. `facade.rs:4993` is `ac_unsatisfy`. Neither takes a note argument, and there is no `ac note` verb.

## So the field has an asymmetric lifecycle

- **Written** only by the v2 ingest path, on a row whose v2 record carried the text.
- **Published** on both faces -- `thread.schema.json` and `schema.graphql`'s `AcStateView.note` -- so every external reader can see it.
- **Not authorable.** An operator working natively in v3 cannot create a note on a criterion, ever.
- **Not editable.** No verb amends one.

A v3-native estate therefore cannot reach a state a migrated estate arrives in, and the two are indistinguishable to a consumer reading the published face. That is the narrower form of the complaint 0133 fixed: 0133 made the state REPRESENTABLE, and representable is not the same as reachable.

## Benign today, and the reason is worth recording

The obvious hazard -- `ac unsatisfy` clearing an ingested note -- **does NOT occur, and this was driven rather than reasoned about.**

`set_ac_state` short-circuits on `*current == state`, and that equality is over the whole value. Before 0133 `Unsatisfied == Unsatisfied` always, so the verb was a guaranteed no-op on an already-unsatisfied row. After 0133 `Unsatisfied { note: Some(x) } != Unsatisfied { note: None }`, so on the page the short-circuit stops applying and the verb looks like it would write, erasing the note.

Driven end to end: `ac_unsatisfy` on an already-unsatisfied row is refused by the TRANSITION MACHINE first (`Err(NotSatisfied)`), so the equality check is never reached and the note survives byte-for-byte.

**The general lesson survives the specific relief: widening an enum changes every `==` on it, including comparisons written long before the new field existed.** Here an undeclared edge happened to guard it. That is luck with a mechanism behind it, not a property anyone chose.

## Not a proposed fix

Whether an authoring verb should exist is a scope question. hv ruled the ingest half on 2026-08-29 and an authoring verb was never in that scope. Filed as a measured edge, not as a request.
